title: What is the RFC 9457 "Problem Details" standard for HTTP errors (`Content-Type: application/problem+json` with `type` [a stable URL the client can switch on], `title`, `status`, `detail` [human-readable], `instance`, plus a `traceId`), how does Spring expose it (`ProblemDetail` / `ErrorResponse`), and why prefer it over a hand-rolled error shape (a documented, framework-supported contract)?
shortTitle: What is the RFC 9457 "Problem Details" standard for HTTP errors

s1_definition.oneliner: RFC 9457 Problem Details is the standard application/problem+json error shape with type, title, status, detail, instance, and extensions, natively supported by Spring's ProblemDetail class.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **RFC 9457** – the IETF standard (replacing RFC 7807) defining a JSON format for HTTP error responses called Problem Details.
- **Media type** – `application/problem+json`, which signals to the client that the body is a standard problem document.
- **Fields** – `type` (a stable URL for client switching), `title` (short summary), `status` (HTTP code in body), `detail` (human explanation), `instance` (URI for this occurrence).
- **Extensions** – custom fields like `traceId` can be added to the standard shape.
- **Spring support** – the `ProblemDetail` class and `ErrorResponse` interface let you build and return problem documents natively.
- **Why standard** – one parser works for all services; new engineers already know it; gateways and tools understand it.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of National Bank of India agreeing with every partner bank on one standard rejection form. Instead of each department inventing its own error slip, everyone uses the same printed form: a reference code box (type), a one-line reason (title), the official rejection stamp number (status), a detailed explanation box (detail), and a case number for this exact rejection (instance). Because it is a standard form, every partner's software already knows how to read it without a custom manual.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         RFC 9457 Problem Details Structure                 │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                          │
│  Content-Type: application/problem+json                  │
│                                                          │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐       │
│  │ type:     "https://api.nbi.in/.../insuf..."  │ ◀─ stable, client switches on this│
│  │ title:    "Insufficient Funds"                │ ◀─ human summary, same per type│
│  │ status:   422                                 │ ◀─ HTTP code in body           │
│  │ detail:   "Balance 250000 < requested 900000"│ ◀─ human, this occurrence      │
│  │ instance: "/api/v1/transfers/req-abc123"      │ ◀─ unique ID for this error    │
│  │ traceId:  "a1b2c3d4"                          │ ◀─ extension: find in logs     │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘       │
│                                                          │
│  Spring Flow:                                            │
│  Exception thrown                                        │
│       │                                                  │
│       ▼                                                  │
│  @RestControllerAdvice                                   │
│  @ExceptionHandler(InsufficientFundsException.class)     │
│       │                                                  │
│       ▼                                                  │
│  ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(422, msg)               │
│  pd.setType(...)                                         │
│  pd.setTitle(...)                                        │
│  pd.setProperty("traceId", ...)                          │
│       │                                                  │
│       ▼                                                  │
│  Return ProblemDetail → Spring sets Content-Type         │
│  automatically to application/problem+json               │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
RFC 9457, replacing RFC 7807, is the IETF standard format for HTTP error responses called Problem Details. The response uses `Content-Type: application/problem+json` and a defined set of fields: `type` is a stable URL identifying the kind of problem and is the field clients switch on; `title` is a short human summary; `status` repeats the HTTP status in the body; `detail` is a human explanation specific to this occurrence; and `instance` identifies this particular occurrence. Extension members like `traceId` can be added.

Spring supports this natively through the `ProblemDetail` class and the `ErrorResponse` interface. You build a `ProblemDetail` with `forStatusAndDetail()`, set the stable type URL, the title, and extension properties, and return it from an exception handler. Spring sets the content type automatically, and with `spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled=true`, even Spring's built-in exceptions produce problem documents.

The reason to prefer it over a hand-rolled shape is that it is a documented, framework-supported contract. At National Bank of India, five microservices each had their own error JSON, so the mobile app carried five separate parsers. Adopting Problem Details meant every service returned the same standard shape, the app used one parser, and new engineers already understood it because it is an IETF standard with library support across languages.

The detail to stress most is that the `type` URL must be stable and is what clients switch on. The `title` and `detail` are human text that can be reworded or localised. Once published, the `type` URL must never change, because it is part of the API contract. That stability is what let the app reliably show an "add money" button for the insufficient-funds type while the team freely improved the human wording.

Remember one sentence: RFC 9457 Problem Details gives every error a standard shape with a stable type URL for client logic and human-readable fields for display, supported natively by Spring's ProblemDetail class.

---

keyPoints: RFC 9457 Problem Details is the IETF standard for HTTP error responses using Content-Type application/problem+json.
The type field is a stable URL that clients switch on; it must never change once published.
The title and detail fields are human-readable and can be reworded or localised without breaking clients.
Extension members like traceId can be added to the standard shape for debugging.
Spring supports Problem Details natively through the ProblemDetail class and ErrorResponse interface.
Adopting the standard means one parser works for all services, eliminating bespoke error shapes.
